$comment: Credential policy, shared by every harness. Two independent halves:
deny_read_paths — refuse reads of credential files before they happen.
redaction       — mask credential material in tool output after the fact.
The second matters more: the danger is not a forbidden command, it is a
REASONABLE command whose output happens to contain a secret. Written after a
real 2026-07-27 incident where an `ansible-vault view | sed` redaction was
simply wrong and ten live credentials landed in a transcript.
Regexes are stored in the intersection of Python `re` and JavaScript RegExp:
numbered groups only (no (?P<x>) / (?<x>)), no verbose mode, [\s\S] instead
of a dotall flag. `flags` carries only portable ones: i, m, s.
Consumers must fail OPEN and LOUD if this file is missing or unparseable —
a redactor that wedges the tool loop is worse than the leak it prevents.

shape_patterns.label: jwt
shape_patterns.note: three base64url segments; catches Home Assistant long-lived tokens

named_assignment.note: Values with NO recognisable shape, caught by the NAME they are bound to. The worst value in the 2026-07-27 leak was a bare hex database password, which every shape rule above misses. Assignment may be `=` (dotenv/shell) or `:` (yaml/json). Groups: 1=name 2=separator 3=value.

benign_value.note: References and placeholders, not live material. Redacting these hides real signal — a MISSING credential would look identical to a set one — and trains the reader to ignore the marker.
